# Music-video storyboard rendering

The C++ renderer ports the current `ezlocalai/VIDEO_UTILS.py` storyboard and
Pythagorean overlay composition. It uses the Pillow 12.3.0 drawing algorithms
adapted to C++, native FreeType/Raqm glyph layout and masks, and ICU for Unicode
case conversion and Python-compatible lyric wrapping. It does not call Python.
The adapted raster code retains Pillow's license in `licenses/Pillow.txt`.

`storyboard_raster_cases.json` contains 330 executions of the actual installed
Pillow 12.3.0: lines, polygons, rectangles, rounded rectangles, ellipses, text
bounds and raster masks, RGB/RGBA, alpha, strokes, multiline text, Latin,
Arabic, Hebrew, Cyrillic, Greek and missing CJK glyphs. Its font hashes and
FreeType 2.14.3/Raqm 0.10.5 versions record the reference toolchain.

`storyboard_composition_cases.json` contains 300 complete images generated by
the actual source helper in the installed Python container. All raw pixel
SHA-256 hashes, dimensions and modes match the native renderer. Cases include
all six phases in generic/theorem mode, overlays, small/odd/invalid dimensions,
Unicode digit dimensions, negative scene indices, empty lyrics, multilingual
titles and lyrics, long words, hyphens, tabs and 100 deterministic randomized
lyric strings. This caught ICU verbose-regex whitespace handling and the
zero-remaining-width long-word behavior of Python's `textwrap`.

Source and capture hashes are embedded in the fixtures. Local captures are
`/tmp/ezlocalai-capture-storyboard-raster.py` and
`/tmp/ezlocalai-capture-storyboard.py`; reference PNGs are retained under
`build/validation/storyboard-raster` and `storyboard-composition`.
Tests compare decoded pixel bytes, not PNG compression bytes. On a mismatch,
the native image is saved to `/tmp/ezlocalai-storyboard-mismatch.png`.

Clean dependency preparation uses CMake and the compiler, without a Python
interpreter. On Ubuntu 24.04 with GCC, CMake, CA certificates, `libfreetype-dev`,
`libharfbuzz-dev`, `libfribidi-dev` and `fonts-dejavu-core` installed:

```
cmake -DDESTINATION="$PWD/build/deps/storyboard" \
  -P cmake/StoryboardDependencies.cmake
cmake -S native -B build \
  -DEZLOCALAI_STORYBOARD_DEPS="$PWD/build/deps/storyboard"
cmake --build build --target test_storyboard --parallel 8
ctest --test-dir build -R '^storyboard_.*_reference$' --output-on-failure
```

The CUDA Dockerfile has an independent `storyboard-dependencies` stage so font
changes do not rebuild model engines. Only native FreeType/HarfBuzz/PNG/Brotli
libraries are extracted from the checksum-pinned upstream wheel. Raqm is
compiled from the pinned Pillow source, linked to those libraries and system
FriBidi; headers, fonts and licenses are copied into the image. DejaVu font
hashes must match the reference. Both image suites run during the CUDA build.

`storyboard_validation.json` records the successful host and CUDA build checks,
a fresh container rerun, source hashes and the retained candidate image.
Production remains on the previously validated LTX image.

The music-video HTTP adapter now uses this renderer when the dependencies
are configured; combined runtime evidence is in `music_video_http_validation.json`.
The rendering comparisons alone do not establish model inference or end-to-end
music-video parity. The renderer
requires the packaged DejaVu fonts; Python's Aileron fallback when both system
font locations are missing is not implemented. Native integer/allocation
limits also differ from Python's extreme-size behavior. The exact-image
claims apply to these captured inputs and pinned libraries.
